utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Mr. Ostreni, the affirmation still applies. Yes, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good morning, General Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, do you recall that it was put to you that you did not produce the rules and regulations of the NLA until after the Ohrid Agreement was signed on the 13th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could please call exhibit P498, page 1, the Rules of Services of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, if we focus on the upper left side of document where there is a stamp with a date.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, can you see the date written above the stamp?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: The date indicates that it is the 2nd of May, 2001. What this date indicates, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the date on which the Rules of Service were completed. It is signed by the commander of the NLA, and it is filed in the archive books.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, with regards to the other rules and regulations, when, on which dates, were they finally produced, signed by the commander of the NLA, and filed, if I can recall, approximately.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first worked on the rules. I assigned duties to people under my control, then I started to work on the formations. So during March and April, the rules and the formations were completed, and I continued to work on other documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: But my question was, General, when were they finally produced, the other rules and regulations. I'm not asking for an approximate date, but for an approximate month, or period, month.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, this rule book was produced in March and April. During the same period of time, I worked on the formation, and I continued to work during May and June on other documents; and as they were completed, I was submitting them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So when these other documents were finally filed? In which month?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly. But, systematically, as I would finish a document, I would submit it to the protocol. Maybe can you see the number better on the protocol.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can you tell us the month, approximately, when you submitted the regulations, the rules, the rest of the regulations and the rules, aside from the one that we see on the screen.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I submitted them systematically, in addition to this one in April; and in May, I submitted the other documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we keep in the same document, can we go to please, to the cover page of this document, to the Rules of Service.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we focus, General, on the lower part of the document, we see your name on the right side. General, by the time that this document was filed on the 2nd of May, 2001, were you already performing your tasks as a Chief of Staff of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We can remove the document from the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, when you were asked about the number of NLA personnel casualties or victims, you testified that the War Veteran Association would have the relevant documents and figures. What is the War Veteran Association, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The War Veteran Association of the NLA was registered as such on the 5th of June, as I remember, 2001, because with -- I apologise, it's 2002, I misspoke. So it was registered as such on the 5th of June, 2002, and the reason why I no longer worked on this was because with the handing over of weapons, the NLA was demobilised, my work finished. At the time, it was quite normal for this association to be formed; and upon request of its members, with its status, with its regulation, it is duty-bound to regulate the issue of the war veterans, and through state associations and political organisations, to resolve the issue of war invalids and the issue of the families of martyrs. In order to be able to deal with this issue and problem, this association has to have the correct number of people who fell as members of the NLA and the details of other citizens who became victim of these fightings.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. I was going to ask you the aim of this organisation, but now I will move on. You just mentioned that this association was registered as such. In which registry, from which country was it registered?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The association was registered at the Tetovo court, and functions as an association with status --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Statute.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And to my recollection, it was registered by an association by this court on 5th of June. There were attempts at the constitutional court to remove this association from the register; but, as I learned, this did not happen. The constitutional court only reaffirmed the decision of Tetovo Court on the registration of the War Veteran Association of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. So I was going to ask you about the issue of war veterans. You mentioned that it was duty-bound to regulate the issue of war veterans. Which war veterans, General, were you talking about?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The veterans who are the members of this association are former members of the NLA. They were members of the NLA until the 26th, when the demobilisation of the NLA occurred.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please call 65 ter 1D956, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this is, I'm afraid, is only in English. It is a US press statement issued by the spokesman of the US Department of State and, it was shown to you by my colleagues. It was released on the 28th of April, 2001. It was read to you, the first two lines: "The United States condemns the attack by armed ethnic Albanian extremists today on Macedonian security forces which resulted in the death of eight Macedonian soldiers." General, is the NLA mentioned as terrorist?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand English, but I can see that the word "extremist" is used there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. You testified that the events which are mentioned in this document happened in the context of clashes between the NLA and the Macedonian security forces and mention, in particular, MX operation. Later on, you mention MX-1 and MX-2. Could you briefly explain these operations carried out by the Macedonian security forces, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The MX operation is the attack, or rather, the operation undertaken by the army and police forces in the area of Tetovo; that is, on the positions where the NLA was positioned. The MX-1 is an operation undertaken against the 113th Brigade, in the Kumanovo area.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, can I stop you a second. When you are explaining the operations, could you please indicate when these operations were carried out, the date, and please go on. Sorry to interrupt you. I'm not asking you for the exact day, just for an approximate date or month, General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will tell you the exact date. The MX operation was carried out on the 25th of March, 2001. MX-1 was on the 28th of March as a continuation of the previous operation, but this time in the Kumanovo area and part of Radusa.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: What about MX-2, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I believe that yesterday you mentioned to my colleague the military operation MX-2. Can you please explain us about this operation and when was carried out?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The MX-2 operation, how I understood it, was a repetition of the MX-1 operation, because the MX-1 failed to eliminate the forces of the 113th Brigade of the NLA, and I think it was carried out on the 8th of May, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, General, if you are aware, which weaponry was used by Macedonian forces? Were they using aircraft, artillery forces?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main weaponry was the artillery one of all kinds, including rocket launchers, multiple-barrel rocket launchers, then infantry forces, helicopters, and aircraft.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And how did the NLA react to these three operations, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The NLA, knowing that the army forces of the Republic of Macedonia had an upper hand, including the police forces --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please repeat his answer. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, sorry to interrupt you. There has been some problems with the translation. Could you please repeat your answer, again, which was not recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The NLA, knowing that the forces of the Republic of Macedonia, the army and the police forces, were superior as they could attack from air and from surface with their artillery and multi-barrel rocket launchers. In its tactics, it implemented the rules on preparing positions in a kind of generic engineers - this is how we call it - so that during the use of artillery from air and surface, the NLA members could be safe in their positions and shelters. During the infantry attacks, it used the weapons that had in its disposal. We had a few Strela 2M rockets and a few anti-aircraft machine-guns, but they could not be used against armoured helicopters.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you just described the weaponry used both by the Macedonian security forces and by the NLA. Do I understand that this weaponry was used with regards to the three operations, or was there some distinction between the weapons used in every single of the three operations that you explained?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The shelling of the NLA positions and the area where the NLA was generally positions was frequent. Almost -- they shelled on a daily basis, because the ARM and the Macedonian police were mainly waging war from distance using helicopters. From time to time, through these operations, they would engage manpower, larger manpower, in order to wipe out the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So, General, were -- was the Macedonian security forces using the same weaponry approximately during the three operations? That was my initial question, General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ARM forces, in all these operations, used artillery sparingly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And what about -- I believe that you mentioned multi-barrel rocket launchers as well as helicopters. Were they used also in the -- in the three operations, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they were used in all three operations. There are details in the book of General Pande Petrovski, who, during MX-2, was informed that there were minefields in the defence area of 112th Brigade, and that's why he ordered for the entire arsenal of the artillery to be used, which probably caused much damage in that area. As a conclusion, he states that no one from his senior officers informed him that they came across mines; in other words, it turned out that this was a pretext for using large artillery forces. It takes 15 to 20 minutes to make the artillery preparations, while the army -- to prepare the tanks, while the army did this for hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you have been mentioning several times the book produced by Pande Petrovski. Do you recall the name of this book, the title of this book, if you do?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall. The title is, "Evidence for the War of 2001." Something along these lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you also mentioned, yesterday, an operation called Vaksince to my learned colleague Mr. Apostolski. In that context, you stated that the Macedonian forces fail. Do you recall giving that evidence, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned the Vaksince operation. Do you want me to give you my comment, my evidence on this operation?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, General. I would like to know when this operation was carried out and how the NLA reacted, counteracted to this operation, where the security forces were defeated?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This operation, to my impression, was prepared during the meeting between Pande Petrovski and General Krstic from Serbia, who was in charge of the area around Bujanovac and Purisevo for this area. So they discussed the possibility of what was going to happen with the forces of the Liberation Army of Presevo, Bujonovac, and Medvedje, after the Serb forces entered this five-kilometre area. According to this agreement, the Serbs were not allowed to do so; but with the opinion of a competent person, they were allowed to enter this area. Krstic expressed his opinion that they would enter until the 25th of May, and a part of UCPMB would cross into Macedonia. So I believe that it was on the 25th of May when this operation was carried out, the operation called Vaksince. It expanded in the entire front of the 115th Brigade from Lojane to the villages down below and, simultaneously, on the north-western part from the direction of Tanuse towards Alasec with the Tactical Group 1. The aim of the operation was not achieved. The 113th Brigade succeeded in defending its positions and in expanding them by penetrating into Haracin as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And what did the NLA forces do to stop, to counter this offensive of the Macedonian security forces?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To defend their positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which weaponry was used?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kalashnikovs, in other words, rifles of different calibre; anti-tank weapon, mainly Zoljas; hand-held grenade launchers RPGs; then we had 60- or 61-millimetre mortars; 82-millimetre mortars; and a few Strela 2M anti-aircraft weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: How was the level of discipline among the NLA soldiers during the operations that you have mentioned, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The level of discipline of the NLA in carrying out combat tasks was very high. Only in this way was the NLA able to stop the penetration of the ARM and police forces and to prevent its extinction.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, I believe that yesterday, and I think that also today, you have mentioned Tactical Group 1 of the 112th Brigade, and I believe that also Operational Tactical Group 2. What did these tactical groups do during the conflict, General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to clarify this. The General Staff of the ARM of the Republic of Macedonia, from the beginning of the war, according to its assessment, carried out a strategic reorganisation of the ARM forces and established the operational tactical groups in Kumanovo and Tetovo, as well as the Tactical Group 1 which operated in the north-western area of the 113th Brigade. These groups were under the command of the Kumanovo corps, and Manastir or Bitola corps. The Kumanovo one directly participated in the command with this units. So there were operational tactical groups and only tactical groups which were of lower level.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, General, we are talking about the NLA, right?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We are talking of the army forces. That's why I explained it to you, thinking that you would take tactical operation and tactical forces as forces belonging to the NLA, which in fact had only brigades.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General, for this clarification. Yesterday, you also mentioned that the NLA did not end up taking Kumanovo. Who instructed the 113th Brigade around Kumanovo not to go any farther, after 5th of July?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that date, we assessed that we had insufficient number of forces to undertake a general operation. Therefore, as the NLA developed and grew, its number grew and every brigade had at least one battalion, enabling the NLA to prepare for undertaking a military operation. The agreement reached on the cease-fire, which took effect on the 6th of July, interrupted all these undertakings; but, at that time, preparations were already done. Every brigade had already taken its tasks, but they were waiting for a specific order of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If the cease-fire agreement had not been reached, the brigades would have gone along with the plans and advance towards Kumanovo?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not towards Kumanova, because that was not part of our plan. We didn't plan to fight within the cities, but we would pass around Kumanova and operate in the communication lines to prevent the coming of the reserve forces of the army in those parts where the NLA was fighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And who issued the order to the brigades not to go along with this plan, General, once the cease-fire was reached?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will simply indicate that this is the second time in the last couple of or three questions that there is a suggestion of an instruction of an order, and we don't think the evidence has been given by the witness on that point, and I think it is quite an important point.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, did you -- was any order issued not to go along, not to advance towards or around Kumanovo after the cease-fire agreement was reached?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the cease-fire agreement was signed, when we gave instructions to brigades to prepare for further actions, we told them to get ready but not to go on attack. They had to wait for a special order by the General Staff, an order which was never given, because, as I said, the cease-fire agreement took effect.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did the NLA comply with the fact that an order was not given; therefore, they had not to go -- they didn't have to go farther?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't [Realtime transcript read in error "did"] go any farther.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please show Exhibit 1D260, and if we could focus on the lower part of the document on the right side.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this is a document which was shown to you by my colleagues, and -- and it's in English; therefore, I'm going to translate it for you. It indicates that the estimates of NLA arm holdings with regards to land-mines is 5.000, which includes anti-personnel and anti-tank mines.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now if we could go, please, to 65 ter 778.19. Just for the record, I believe that the answer of the witness in page 12, line 1 was not recorded properly, and it reads: "They did go any farther." I believe the witness said: "They didn't go any farther."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That was my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you were also shown this document by my colleagues. This is a document that you testified was given to you by the NATO from the operation Task Force Harvest, once the operation was finished. And if we look at item 6, it indicates that the number of mines and grenades collected by the NATO forces reached the figure of 1045. You indicated that grenades could be also 60-millimetres or 80-millimetres grenades. General, is this the document which was given to you by the NATO forces after the operation was ended?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P519, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please call Exhibit 1D272. It's former 65 ter 317. Do we have a Macedonian version of this document? No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we will have to work with the English. I'm going to translate to you what it says. I apologise. This is an order, issued by the Chief of Staff of the armed forces Pande Petrovski, on the 5th of July, 2001, and bears the title, "Very urgent: Cease-fire for all weapon, planting mines, and other improvised explosive devices." General, this order indicates on item 1: "On the 6th of July, 2001, at 0001 hours, a cease-fire for all weapons, planting mines, and other improvised explosive devices will come on power." General, to whom the Chief of Staff of the Macedonian army was allowed to issue, to address this order?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment otherwise than to his forces. He has already addressed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. General, I just read to you that one of the points he was ordering actually is the cease-fire for all weapons, planting mines, and explosive devices. General, can we conclude that the Macedonian security forces had this weaponry among their assets?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what the order says. I don't want to testify here by attacking someone else. I only want to testify to what I know. The Chief of General Staff of the Macedonian army says that he bans the use of mines, which shows that other plans must have been in place for using them before; but this is an analysis which I would not make in my capacity as a witness here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General, I appreciate that. In item 5 of this document, General, it indicates: "In case of self-defence to be responded to the fire and informed OSCE and NATO." Then farther down, it indicates: "The retaliation is not self-defence and would represent breaking of the cease-fire." General, here it seems that General Petrovski states that cease-fire can be somehow broken in case of self-defence but not retaliation. Did this general rule also apply to the NLA cease-fire; meaning, could the NLA respond upon being attacked?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The cease-fire, as you might understand, in this case, is an order he has given to his forces; but before that order, there is an agreement which regulates in more details the state of affairs. This is where he got the material to draw up this order. In this agreement, point 7, 5 says that the cease-fire shouldn't be used in order to improve the once situation both in defence or in attack. That is why the NLA had informed NATO of their position, and had promised to stop the use of weapons at the time that the cease-fire was in force. But in case of being attacked in those lines which were already made known to the monitors, they, of course, had the right to defend themselves, and I believe that the ARM had the same rights, in case they were attacked by the NLA forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. Yesterday, I showed to you Exhibit P481 which was a resolution from the president of Macedonia, dated the 5th of August, 2001. In that resolution the president order to undertake measures to enter Tetovo to prevent its fall within NLA authority. General, I asked you a rather broad question which was whether you were aware of fighting going on in Tetovo in 2001. Let me be a bit more precise, a bit more specific, General. Can you recall whether there were clashes between Macedonian security forces and NLA around 8, 9, 10 August, 2001, prior to the signing of the Ohrid Agreement in or around Tetovo?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 5th of August, during the time that order you put to me was issued, it had to do with the preparation of an operation which aimed at taking Tetovo and freeing Tetovo-Jazince road, if I might say so. This is how I understood that instruction and the operation that would follow, based on that. They prepared for that, for that operation, of course, and attempts were made. In fact, the troops started to move, the troops of the army, towards Tetovo on the 8th. A clash ensued in Karpalak area, which, at the time, the NLA, the commander and myself, were not clear to which -- which carried out that operation. Then, on the 9th, there was another operation launched against Brigade 115 in Radush, which lasted on the 10th as well, with an intervention in Poroj village by the ARM or police forces, I'm not sure which. Then, after the 10th, on the 12th, the Ljuboten incident happened. In my opinion, there were a number of actions, preparations, attempts made to create higher tension, to prevent the signing of the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. General, what do you recall about these operation, these clashes in and around Tetovo on the 8th, 9th, and 10th of August?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The aim --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you wait please. Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think that, again, the counsel has to be careful. The question was very leading the first time around, and the witness has been careful to respond to what he knew about the, what he called, operations, by indicating the events which he knew about. He hasn't given any evidence to the effect of clashes in or around the Tetovo area, and that's, in our submission, the Your Honour, the second time that it is a very leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There's some substance in that Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I will rephrase my question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, I will rephrase my question. Can you recall whether, around the 8th, 9th, and 10th of August, 2001, there were clashes -- whether there were clashes in or around Tetovo on those dates, between the NLA and the Macedonian security forces?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interfering with my colleague's questioning; but as far as I recall, the witness expressly stated yesterday that there were no clashes in Tetovo in August. So I believe that this is an inappropriate question for the witness to answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps you could clarify your preliminary ground there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I may clarify. I thought that my question asked yesterday actually was quite broad as it encompassed the whole month of August, and now I was trying to focus actually to a particular day which I thought could give the witness some clarity about my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: An answer that there were no clashes in August would include no clashes on any particular day.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: But it could also imply after the Ohrid Agreement, Your Honour, and I was trying to be more specific about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may explore that area but without leading.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So, General, are you aware of any clashes, if there were, in or around Tetovo, before the signing of the Ohrid Agreement between the NLA and the Macedonian security forces, if you know?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of any such clashes in Tetovo. I know that there was this instance of Karpalak on the 8th of August. I also know that fighting took place between Brigade 115 on the 9th and the 10th in Radusa area.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. May I help to refresh your memory if I show you some documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could please call 65 ter 284, page 8. It's within the range N001-8730, page 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness did not say that he didn't recall, so I see no need for my colleague to refresh his memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We would like to put to the witness to show him some extracts which have been shown in this courtroom with regards to the events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: With a view to him changing his present evidence, is that what you're doing?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. He has given his evidence. It is with a view to comment on the documents that we're going put forward to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are these documents that have been dealt with so far in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not with this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, how do they arise for re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We are trying to explore about when - in cross-examination, Your Honour, as a matter of fact - there arose the issue that cease-fire was broken by both parties. Therefore, along these lines, Your Honour, we were trying to explore that in which context, in which cases the cease-fire agreement was breached, was violated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That much seems legitimate, yes, and that's what you are now attempt to do. Very well. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, can you please focus on the first paragraph, the first full paragraph, just below the date, Skopje, 9 August 2001. I will read to you what it says, General: "The situation in the area of Tetovo is deteriorating considerably. As before, the town of Tetovo is predominantly under the control of the NLA. Since about five hours, serious battle have again been developing in or around Tetovo. "Heavy weapons such as mortars and artillery (only the Macedonian military forces) have been deployed on both sides. The NLA seems to be concentrated at the Kuzman barracks. The Macedonian forces are operating from, among other places, artillery positions on the other side of route club towards Kaleberg." General, does this document help you to recall that the cease-fire agreement was, indeed, breached with regards to Tetovo on the 9th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was such a conflict. With the participation of the monitors and the NLA commanders, all these places -- forces that had breached the cease-fire in some places were withdrawn, and the cease-fire was restored.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. General, can you recall when the forces withdrew from Tetovo, if you do?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that this happened very quickly, after they penetrated, because after the 9th, there is this operation which involved Brigade 115, and it affected also the area covered by Brigade 114. So the commitment of the commander, Ali Ahmeti, was to make sure that the situation was restored back to normal, and the forces which went as far as the Tetovo barracks withdrew. I don't recall, accurately, if that happened on that day or on the next day.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was any order issued by yourself or by Ali Ahmeti to withdraw from Tetovo, if there was such an order?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was given by Ali Ahmeti orally, because at that time he was in person, there, at the brigade. He ordered them orally to restore the situation back to normal, to withdraw the forces, and allow the cease-fire to remain in force, in order to reach the phase of the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was this order complied with by the brigades, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they withdrew; otherwise, we wouldn't have come up to the moment when we signed the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We can remove the document from the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, in wartime, an army convoy, an NLA convoy, or a police station, or a NLA headquarters or barracks would be a military target?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are military targets.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, it was put to you that the NLA acted in a hit-and-run fashion, and you denied it. You testified that you, the NLA, had been involved in an active defence, rather than retreats or hit-and-run attacks. What did you mean with "active defence," General, and could you give some example, please.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that we had almost permanent positions which were known, something which make it possible to monitor the situation and follow up the implementation of the cease-fire by the monitors of the competent bodies, including the NATO forces. We defended ourselves; and as brigades grew, it set up their relevant unit, expanded the territory under its control, and advanced. In this way, systematically, it enhanced its authority over the territory it controlled. In this way, we didn't use the hit-and-run style attacks, which might have been used in other instances, because, in this way, we would inflict huge losses, human losses to ourselves which was not our objective. Our objective was to make sure that we had as few casualties as we possibly could, until we reached the political agreement. So we didn't change our positions. Brigade 113 developed from Tanuse continuously until those positions that I gave to NATO; Brigade 112 from Gur i Kuq on towards, until it reached the positions that I also gave to NATO; and this applies to all the other brigades. I don't want to take your time by recounting all of that. So it was engaged in an active defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, it was also put to you that the NLA scared civilians off in Aracinovo once the NLA had exercised its authority over the town. You were also asked several times about the so-called "ethnic cleansing" allegedly committed by the NLA. You answer: "It was war, and the civilians were scared of war. What did you mean with that answer, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to say that any person in a territory where weapons are being fired, where clashes between two sides occur, of course those persons would be scared.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And which could be a natural consequence of this situation, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Could you please clarify.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I will move on, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please show Exhibit 1D259.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this is a document that, I believe, it was showed to you by my colleague. It refers to June 2001, and it was provided to our colleagues by an embassy here in The Hague. The first -- actually, in the heading, we can read that: "This is an information record not finally evaluated intelligence."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could go to the second page, please, and if we could focus in the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this paragraph was read to you, and the last three lines were actually omitted. I will read it, for the record, the full paragraph: "According to local inhabitants, sometime during the afternoon of Friday, 8 June, approximately 30 members of the NLA entered the town and began scaring inhabitants out of the town, especially the ethnic Macedonian inhabitants." Then the paragraph goes on: "The police reaction was to establish roadblocks, closing the main vehicular routes into or out of the village and, in effect, surrendering the town to the NLA." General, which are the consequences of this measures taken by the police; meaning, closing the routes in and out of the village?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I would kindly ask you to tell me which village or town is in question, because the text is in English and I don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I believe that they are talking about Aracinovo. Do you want me to repeat my question, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you asked me which was the reason for erecting these roadblocks, if I'm not mistaken; or maybe that -- repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I was asking which would be the consequences of basically cutting off the routes in or out of the village, with regards to the civilian population, by the police, by the police of the Macedonian forces?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would be under police control, the control that they had at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: They? Who do you mean by "they," General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who erected those roadblocks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, my question was whether when the police basically build some roadblocks, cuts the way in and out of the village of Aracinovo in this case, what would be a consequence with regard to the civilian population who want to leave the village?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have negative consequences. It would cause fear among the population, but it wouldn't be proper for me to comment on these newspapers. Newspapers describe many events like this at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. You also -- it was put to you that intimidation or scaring of civilians was taking place in almost all places where the NLA was active. You answer in one particular question that: "The 113th Brigade received several ultimatums from the Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Defence, so that the civilian population could move out from the village." What did you mean with that answer, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was not just one ultimatum. They ultimatums had two directions: One, they wanted the NLA members to abandon their positions, to throw their weapons, and surrender to the police; and, two, the population to move out. They were given time. Unless that was not respected, the shelling, the combat would continue. It was my impression that the army was to be released from its duty in order -- if the civilians did not leave; and, at the same time, there was a propaganda launched, according to which the NLA was accused of using the civilians as human shields against the army attacks, and this was not true at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Why was this not true at all, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those civilians had their own sons, daughters, husbands, sisters, brothers amongst the ranks of the NLA, and that's why at the time I issued a statement for the public, saying that this was not true. I added that why would we wage a war if we kill our own children, our own brothers and sisters. Through this statement, I appealed to the media to go to the location, to see and talk to the citizens, and to find out the truth for themselves. Then there was a video-clip, some journalists talking to civilians in the basements, and the civilians stated that they will never abandon their houses. I didn't want to add anything to this because that would make the situation more severe, and I don't think it would contribute to -- to the goal.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please call Exhibit 1D19, 1D1-9.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, I apologise, because this document is only in English; therefore, I will read to you the relevant parts. This is an OSCE report regarding human rights development and covers the period 1 to 15 August 2001. You have been asked in cross about actions allegedly perpetrated by the NLA like, as I mentioned scaring off population, beatings, looting, damage to religious facilities, or kidnappings. This was particular document was read to you, but only parts of it. I'm going to read to you the missing parts.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we focus in the first paragraph, starting with the first paragraph, it will be the fifth line.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: It reads: "Attitudes in both communities have hardened further, and both security forces and civilians have become more aggressive towards members of the perceived opposing ethnic group." General, is this statement a more accurate reflection of the situation in Macedonia at the time of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such situations not as of 1st of August. I have mentioned so many times during my evidence that I'm handicapped here, since I don't speak English. The interethnic relations were deteriorating and the situation was more tense. This would be my short answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In the third paragraph General, and I am going to try to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. The question of my colleague was: "Is this statement a more accurate reflection of the situation in Macedonia at the time of the conflict?" I was just wondering whether it could be clarified, more accurate than what.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I believe, Your Honour, that the witness testified that the interethnic relations were deteriorated and the situation was more tense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. You may understand the witness one way. I think it is not altogether clear what he is saying. You may need to clarify it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, could you please clarify: What did you mean with your answer that the interethnic relations were deteriorating and the situation was becoming more tense at that time?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that the trust between the two ethnicities was diminishing. There were contributions to this by the very fact that weapons were distributed by the police for their self-defence, and the situation became more tense. People began to lose their faith that the Ohrid Agreement was ever going to be signed and that the war was ever going to end. The clashes that we spoke about, in Tetov, in Karpalak, the fighting at Radush on the 9th and 10th of August, all these contributed to the deterioration of the situation, that signals were being sent to the population that perhaps the Ohrid Agreement was never going to be reached.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. When my colleagues put to you this alleged acts committed by the NLA, you mentioned that also the Albanian population had been victims or targets of this -- of similar actions. If we focus in the same page in paragraph 3, and I'm going to read it to you, General: "In addition to criminal acts by disorganised groups that are best described as mobs or vigilantes, there has been an increasing behaviour outside areas of engagement that is historical associated with paramilitary formations. "The most serious such incident occurred on August 8 in the village of Rashtani near Veles. During the late hours of the night, one of two ethnic Albanian homes in the village was fired upon by automatic weapons. An 11-year-old boy was wounded in the gun-fire and died." The last line of this paragraph, General, reads: "The ethnic Albanian families have reportedly left the village as a result of this incident." General, with regard to this particular event, why is the Albanian population leaving the villages?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in English. I can see it now. It is an assessment by the body that you mentioned. I believe that they left out of fear, insecurity, because they didn't know what was going to happen to them the next day.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: From the paragraph that I read, General, did you understand that there was any kind of NLA involvement in these actions?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no NLA in Veles. You are talking of a village in the municipality of Veles, which is towards the centre of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could turn to the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, it was also put to you that there was a decline of discipline with regards to the NLA. If we focus on the second paragraph of this page, and, again, I'm going to read it to you, General. I apologise that it is not in Albanian. This OSCE document reads: "There are disturbing indications of a decline in the discipline and professionalism of the main forces of both combatants." General, according to this report, was this decline of discipline, of professionalism, involving only the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You read it, and as I understood it, it's between the fighting parties. It does not mention only the NLA, if I understood your reading of the document correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, General, you were also asked about kidnappings allegedly carried out by the NLA. If we focus on the fourth paragraph of this report, the paragraph that starts with "The mission." The paragraph, General, reads: "The mission continues to highlight the plight of the missing and detained. Both sides deny having detainees; however, clearly both sides do hold such persons. The total number of missing and detained persons is impossible to establish, but may well be in the hundreds. "It is often impossible to investigate reports of kidnaps and detentions, both because of lack of cooperation from local authorities and because of the seriously [sic] security situation." General, is this report talking about detainees taking only by the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please read it again. I'm not clear because I don't know what it exactly says, this report. I really don't remember now whether it mentioned both parties or only the NLA. Could you please read it again to me, that part.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, General. "The mission continues to highlight the plight of the missing and detained. Both sides deny having detainees; however, clearly both sides do hold such persons." Do you want me to repeat my question, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There is no need for that. "Both sides." The text report refers to both sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please go to 65 ter 1D745, please, and if we could focus on the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this is the record of a meeting of the European Commission on Kidnapped and Missing Persons, which was shown to you by my colleague. The first paragraph reads: "The commission continues its effort to find out the fate of the 20 missing persons. In connections with both the Ministry of Interior and the former NLA, we are now trying to clarify a number of questions that both parties have been unable to answer so far." General, is the commission having inquiries with regards to unsolved questions involving both the NLA and the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I understand it, it involves both sides and all the missing persons whose fates remain unknown.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please go to Exhibit 1D268. It's former Rule 65 ter 1D828.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this is, again, a document only in English. It's an OSCE report. A fortnightly OSCE report from the 24th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could go please to page 5, the ERN of the page is 1D00-7226, and if we could focus on the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you were asked several times about alleged destructions of religious sites with regards to the NLA, and you mentioned, you testified that also mosques had been destroyed, burned down by the Macedonian security forces. If we read this first line: "The mission has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting the questioning by my colleague. I don't think that Mr. Ostreni, at any stage, suggested that a mosque had been burned down by the security forces. I think he has indicated, and the question would be fair to be put, that he said, as I recall, that the Macedonian forces had, indeed, damaged a number of religious properties as well. But I do not the recall, and I would stand corrected if that's the case, if he suggested that one had been burned down counsel by the security forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: 7580, the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, please, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General this document reads: "The mission has followed closely the effect of the fighting on religious and cultural sites. The destruction of the Lesok monetary, and previously that of the mosque in Prilep, appear to be the first major cases of deliberate targeting of sites." General, was the mosque in Prilep one of the sites that you were referring to in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe I mentioned that the mosque was damaged. There were other mosques that suffered damages. I didn't mention all of them. I have information and the competent organs who followed this have information, as well as the Islamic community and the orthodox community have this information. So I didn't deem it necessary to find all the names of damaged mosques for the purpose of my evidence here, but it is true that damages were --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Mosques were damaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have two more questions with regard to this document. I don't know if you wish me to stop here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If you could go, please, to the page 6, the next page, and focus on the second full paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this report reads as follows: "The issue of illegally detained persons continues to be highly emotive and politically sensitive. EAAG is alleged to hold anywhere from 30 to 50 persons, although it is believed that the actual figure is in the lower end of the scale. There are also allegations that the government is holding persons without due process." General, do you recall the fact that the government, in August, was holding persons without due process. Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had information for -- from the press and the media that I followed. Of course, I didn't have first-hand information on this matter. I have a friend who has gone through the maltreatment of the police. His name is Zini Tala. He was taken by the police and driven around with a sack on his head. He then was returned home, but I think he still has consequences.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we can move to the last paragraph of the same page.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, I believe that you testified that the NLA shut down, closed houses of prostitution. This paragraph reads: On a more positive note, the combination of armed conflict and apparent actions of the EAAG to close houses of prostitution appears to have resulted in a significant decline in the number of trafficked women in the western portion of the country?" General, is this paragraph a reflection of what you testified in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now and resume at five minutes past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. Could we please call Exhibit P494, page 18.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, it was put to you on several occasions that the NLA did not want, did not support the territorial integrity of Macedonia, and you testified in the negative, that indeed among the NLA demands was always to maintain the integrity and sovereignty of the country. You mentioned several times the proposal of the Macedonian Academy of Sciences and Arts. The document that you will see in the screen, General - and, again, I apologise - is in English. It's an ICJ, International Crisis Group, Balkans report with the title, "Macedonia: Last chance for peace." It was produced the 20th of June, 2001. I'm going to read to you, General, some extracts of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Just, if we could, please, scroll down a little bit, so we focus in the - yeah, that's perfect; thanks a lot - on the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Just below the title, "The Prime Minister's hidden agenda," we can read: "On the 29th May 2001, one of the Macedonia's state owned (politically controlled) newspapers caused a storm by publishing details of a proposal, emerging reportedly from the Macedonian Academy of Sciences and Arts, to solve the crisis by agreeing a territorial and population exchange with neighbouring Albania. "The partition was envisaged that the three largest ethnic Albanian majority cities in western Macedonia could be annexed to Albania. Macedonia's quid pro quo will be a small strip of land in Albania with access to the Adriatic Sea." General, is this the proposal that you mentioned several times in cross-examination and, indeed, in communique, Exhibit P510, one of your communiques?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour. Your Honours, the existence of this document has not been established. This is an unverified fact; therefore, we have doubts about the veracity of this text.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is currently an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I believe it is an exhibit, Mr. Apostolski. Yes. Do you mean the plan behind it?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean the plan of the Macedonian Academy of Sciences and Arts, which was allegedly prepared and which allegedly existed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And which was allegedly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness is speaking about his understanding about that, Mr. Apostolski. So please continue, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It doesn't mean to say what the witness understands is necessarily the truth or reliable. The witness can only give his understanding of the matter. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, was this proposal, which was published in a newspaper in Macedonia, the one that you were referring in your testimony and also in one of your communiques?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, this is what I was referring to. It was published in the newspaper, and I refer to it as it was published.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which was the position of the NLA with regards to this proposal?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The position of the NLA was and is the territorial integrity and dependence [as interpreted] of Macedonia. They should be maintained. They are inalienable.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. I'm going to read to you the third paragraph of this document, the third line, starting, "On the 31st of May." "On the 31st of May, the plan was presented in the other state-controlled Macedonian language newspaper, Nova Makedonija, this time with a more ambitious map implicating Bulgaria in the scheme. "The reactions of the government leaders did nothing to allay suspicions of VMRO-DPMNE complicity in publishing, if not originating the partition of the plan."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, Which was the position of the government with regards to this proposal, if you know?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the position of the government at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. In the same paragraph, it reads -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I will move on to the next page, if we could go.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: The article reads in the first paragraph: "Fantasies of territorial partition involving the mass deportation of ethnic Albanians have been part of Macedonian nationalist subculture for decades. What was new in this episode was the semi-explicit official in [indiscernible] given to the plan and also the timing. "The timing seemed intended to accomplish three things: To gain leverage for full Macedonian concessions, by moving the starting point to the far right nationalist positions; to raise the stakes with the NLA; and to shore up the prime minister's ratings among the VRMO-DPMNE's rank and file supporters." The third paragraph reads: "The ethnic Albanian leaders immediately rejected the proposal." General, were you aware of the position of the Albanian political parties with regards of this proposal?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We said that we do not reconcile with any partitioning of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I'm referring also to the -- the text reads: "Ethnic Albanian leaders." I'm also referring to the Albanian political parties. Would you -- are you aware of the position of the political, Albanian political parties in Macedonia, with regards to this proposal?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the contacts that Mr. Ali Ahmeti had with Albanian political parties, I didn't have any information that they wanted, that they were in favour of this partitioning. Even in the Prizren agreement, one of the important points is a preservation of the territorial integrity and sovereignty of the Republic of Macedonia. Based on this, I assume that the parties had the same stance that they expressed in the Prizren agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. The fourth of this document ...

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could please scroll down, so we can see the fourth and the fifth paragraph. That's perfect. Thanks a lot.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: ... reads: "In a nationally televised interview, on 3 June, the prime minister offered the mandate to the social democrats for the changes to the constitution, because his party, VRMO-DPMNE, has made it clear that either we create the constitution made to measure for the Albanians or we'll have war. "This should be made clear to everyone. The position of the VRMO-DPMNE is that we categorically refuse any dialogue in such an environment." The first three line of the next paragraph reads: "The interview shocked many Macedonians because it seemed to confirm that Georgievski had rejected any idea of trying to reach a peaceful resolution through political reforms." General, would that statement, that position of Georgievski be an accurate reflection of his denial to engage in a dialogue?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I didn't know anything about that. I was engaged in the professional aspect of the NLA. I, of course, followed political developments; but if it's written as you are putting to me, then I would agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please call document with the following ERN. It's N006-6508, and we have hard copies of this document for the Chamber, the witness, and the colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have the 65 ter number from our colleague.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux is well aware that this is not a 65 ter document. It was provided by the witness during proofing, and it was disclosed to the Defence on the 1st of November. It was given to us on the 31st of October, and provided, disclosed to the Defence on the 1st of November. This is, Your Honour, the Prizren agreement which has been mentioned during all the evidence in chief and in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm a little curious. Are you saying this is the agreement, or is it some commentary on the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: No. This is the agreement, Your Honours, as provided by the witness, the text of the agreement. The Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I, Your Honour, speak?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue will ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, it was put to you that prior -- that prior to the Ohrid Agreement, the NLA was never regarded as a valid negotiating partner. You testified that, indeed, you reached an agreement with international representatives in Aracinovo, as well as with the cease-fire, and you, indeed, refer to the Prizren agreement. I would like to go through the document with you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We'll keep the objection, if any, to the admission of this document. It is sought to be tendered, but the counsel has indicated, I believe, that there was an agreement reached with international representatives. As the document itself made clear, to the extent there was agreement between anyone, this would have been agreement between the representative of two Albanian political parties and Mr. Ahmeti. I think what happened in this occasion is there was a facilitator who was an international, but the evidence has not been led whether he agreed or that he represented anyone in relation to those negotiation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am not sure if I -- maybe I have not been clear. I was just simply -- obviously, this agreement was reached between the Albanian parties leaders and Ali Ahmeti. I was just referring to prior evidence that this witness gave with regards to the NLA being acknowledged as a negotiating partner, with regards to the Aracinovo, with regards to the cease-fire, and this third agreement which, indeed, did not involve international representatives; only Albanian political parties. I'm sorry if it didn't come across clear in my introduction. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, in the first paragraph of this document, we read that: "The Albania leaders in Macedonia, Ali Ahmeti, political representative of the NLA; Arben Xhaferi, president of the DPA; and Imer Imeri, president of the PDP, in the name of the subjects that they are representing, have agreed with a common action about the issues of a wider, national, and social consensus, which needs to reform the Republic of Macedonia in the way that it becomes a democratic state." General, Were these parties, Ali Ahmeti met and the representatives of these two political party, the ones who participated and, indeed, agreed with the Prizren document?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, if we move to the second paragraph - and, indeed, the whole document lays out the different demands that the three negotiating parties put forward in the document - in the third line, we can read: "The aim to keep the integrity and the multi-ethnic character of Macedonia, while not accepting any ethnic territorial, military solution." Was this aim among the goals of the NLA, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was; and as you see, it is expressed here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: A bit farther down, it mentions: "As well as pretending that the process of the transformation of the Republic of Macedonia need to be directed towards the Euro-Atlantic integrations and the acknowledgment that the solution will be found within a national political process with the USA and EU facilitation." General, was the NLA supporting the involvement of the international community as mediators, facilitators to end the conflict?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. This is shown in all our communiques.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we move to the next paragraph, it reads: "Based on these principles, the Albanian leaders in Macedonia are making a decision to take part in the process of the reformist dialogue, while engage for the change of the preamble of the constitution of Macedonia with which the Albanians will achieve the status of state founders." General, was also the NLA demanding the change of the preamble of the constitution?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: A bit farther down, it indicates, and I quote: "The use of the Albanian language as a second official language in Macedonia; for ethnic proportional reputation in the state institutions; widening the competences in the self-government; a complete secularisation of the constitution, state; establishing the consensual democracies for the issues that are connected to the national rights, which means limitation of the process of outvoting in the areas which are directly involved with the ethnic rights." Were these issues - the use of the Albanian language as a second official language, an ethnic proportional representation in the state institutions, a widening of the competences in the self-government, and also the secularisation of the goals - among demands of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were demands by the UNL, and completed by the demands of the political parties. We added that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Finally, General, in the last paragraph, it is indicated: "Also within this debate are the measures for transformation of the life of the NLA members in different forms of civic professions, while also cover those of within the government institutions." There are some references below to a complete rehabilitation of the NLA members, the building of villages and family economies, and taking care of victims of war. General, is this text also a reflect of the NLA demands at that time?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that meeting, when they decided to sign the Prizren agreement, these are part of it. They agreed, the signatories to this agreement, agreed also on these issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, I believe that you mentioned the date of this agreement when you testified in-chief, but could you please repeat it, if you know, the date when the parties made and agreed on this document?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this moment, it doesn't come to my mind. You would have helped me if you mentioned a date, and I would say simply "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid I cannot do, General. But if you don't recall, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have mentioned it earlier as the 26th, I think, but I don't know whether it was May or June.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please display in the screen N006-6506.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, can you explain to the Chamber what is this document?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is taken from Fakti newspaper I think, and the photo has been taken after the agreement of Mr. Ali Ahmeti, Imer Imeri, and Arben Xhaferi following the agreement. It contains the date you asked me about, the 25th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please read, for the record, the title of this document, as we don't have an English translation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I believe the Defence has never seen this document, in any case not in an English translation, nor did we have an indication of the fact that the document would be used. We are, therefore, in an awkward situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: This document was disclosed to the Defence, again, on the 1st of November. There is no English translation, neither for the Defence nor for us. As I mentioned, it was given by us -- it was given to us by the witness during proofing. We didn't use it in-chief because we thought to give to the Defence a fair amount of time to be prepared, which is now 15 days. So they had the document, Your Honours, during the whole cross-examination and, the issues which are mentioned in this document arise in cross-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, let's be clear, Ms. Regue, that if the Prosecution was proposing go rely on it, it should have advanced it as part of its evidence in chief; and if was the case that there had not been adequate notice given at that time, that should have been faced and dealt with then. So it's not relevant that, because of a late discovery or disclosure of the document, that you didn't deal with it in the course of your examination-in-chief. Now, having made that clear, you say the subject matter - I'm not, at the moment at all familiar with the content of the document - you say that the subject matter has been dealt with in the course of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, can I clarify that. In evidence in chief, indeed, questions regarding this document were asked to the witness; and, in the content of this document, the witness gave his evidence about that. I mean that is in the transcript about the Prizren agreement. At that moment, we didn't seek to tender the document because we thought that it was fair for the Defence to give them more time. That was the only purpose. So in the evidence in chief, indeed, the issue was dealt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is your present objective in turning to this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, to show that, indeed, the NLA was regarded as a valid, negotiating partner at that time in 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that is the evidence that has been given by this witness; and now this is, what, a newspaper report, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I was going to ask the witness actually what was the content of this newspaper report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This is a newspaper report.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: This one, this document in the screen, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And it's simply a report about --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: The agreement, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- a meeting at Prizren, which it is said an agreement was reached. Is that really going to advance your case?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I was just simply trying to authenticate the date and the fact that this meeting took place. It was only purpose of showing this newspaper, which was going to take theoretically ten seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I do believe that the present evidence is that the matter was the subject of newspaper reports at the time, and you are simply putting to the witness one newspaper report. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I was going to ask him simply which was the content of this newspaper report, briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I think that may be going too far.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In order to corroborate, Your Honour, as a matter of fact, the fact that the meeting took place and the agreement was reached, that was the only purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, you would be allowed to put to the witness to confirm what I think is his earlier evidence that there were newspaper reports and that appears to be one of them, but I don't think you ought to go into further detail in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I was not going to do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I was just intending to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: -- put that forward, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, were you aware, do you recall if the meeting in Prizren and the agreement was published in the media in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was published in the Fakti newspaper; and in the Macedonian newspapers, it was spoken much about it in the newscasts, saying that Imeri and Xhaferi have betrayed the newly formed government, broad coalition government. So there was lot of debate going on, but I don't have accurate information on all the newspaper articles. This was something I knew, and there was the publication of the entire text of the Prizren agreement, in another newspaper, containing all the signatures.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can you recall the date of the agreement, having seen the newspaper now?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see the date here, the 25th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's written also in my personal documents; but, at the moment, it escaped my memory.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.
