utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We can remove this document from the screen. And if we could please call ERN N006-6502. Again, advancing Mr. Mettraux's question, this is not a 65 ter document, Your Honour. It is also a document which was given to us during proofing, disclosed to the Defence on the 1st of November, dealt in-chief and also in cross-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, it was put to you that the Ohrid Agreement was a rejection of the NLA existence and actions, and was aimed at undermining the goals of the NLA. You testified that that was not the case, that the Ohrid Agreement reflected the Prizren agreement, communique number 6, and also a memorandum.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have hard copy of this communique, if you wish, and also for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would simply indicate for the record that it would have been nice had we been given an indication that these document would be used prior to re-examination. We have, indeed, received the document in question a couple of weeks ago, I believe, but not an indication that this would be used at this stage in any case.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I believe that in re-examination the documents that we are supposed to use, it also raises from the issues dealt in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, if we look at this communique number 6, if we move to the second paragraph, it reads: "The NLA is for keeping of the territorial integrity of Macedonia. The NLA demands are the demands of the entire Albanian people in Macedonia." Again, General, the territorial integrity is mentioned here. Item 1 reads: "International neutral mediation in the conflict." Item 2: "The census of the population to be made by an international, neutral institution, and the citizenship to be recognised to all of the residents." Item 3: "Change of the constitution." Item 4: "Macedonia to be a state of two nations; Albania, Macedonian, respectively. This will enable that all the injustices that are made to the Albanian people by the ethnic Macedonian to disappear." Then there is a list of discrimination in different aspects of the public life. General, is this communique an accurate description of the NLA demands?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please show P84, which is the Ohrid Agreement. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this is the Ohrid Framework Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: It's dated the 13th of August, 2001. Item 1 of the Ohrid Framework Agreement reads, "Basic principles," and then item 1.2 indicates: "Macedonian sovereignty and territorial integrity." General, was this, the Macedonian sovereignty and territorial integrity, a demand which was reflected in the Prizren and in the communique number 6?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Item 1.3 mentions: "The multi-ethnic character of Macedonian society must be preserved and reflected in public life." Again, General, is this a demand reflected both in Prizren and in communique number 6?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Item 1.5 mentioned: "The development of local self-government is essential for encouraging the participation of citizens in democratic life and for promoting respect for the identity of communities." Again, General, is mentioned in the Prizren agreement the need for a widening of the local self-government?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In item 2.1, it is mentioned that: "The parties underline the importance of the commitments of July 5th, 2001. There shall be a complete cessation of hostilities, a complete voluntary disarmament of the ethnic armed Albanian armed groups." General, was this disarmament referring to the operation, the plan Harvest, which was implemented afterwards?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Item 3, General, reads: "Development of decentralised government," and item 3.1 mentions: "A revised law on local self-government." Again, General, this demand for a widening of self-government, was it enclosed within the Prizren agreement?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more competencies for the self-government.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Point 3.2 reads: "Boundaries of municipalities will be revised within one year of the completion of a new census, which will be conducted under international supervision." General, was the need for a new census with intervention of international parties foreseen in communique number 6?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in item 2 of the communique number 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could please go to the next page. Scroll up a little bit. Thanks a lot. Also in the English version, if we could scroll up. Actually, turn to the next page. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Point item number 4 of the Ohrid Framework Agreement mentions the mentions: "A non-discrimination and equitable reputation. Item 4.2 mentions: "Laws relating employment in public administration will include measures to assure equitable representation of communities in all central and local public bodies." General, was the demand for an end of discrimination and equal representation for ethnic minorities foreseen in communique number 6 and in the Prizren agreement?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in item 3, changes to the constitution and force Macedonia to become a state of two peoples of equal peoples. And further down, it says that this would be contribute to eliminating the distinctions between the ethnicities, non-discrimination, removal of discrimination in all walks of life in the administration, and so on. So I don't want to mention every single detail, but, in one word, it is mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Item 5, with the title, "Special parliamentary procedures." Item 5 foresees "constitutional amendments" in item 5.1. Also, item 5.2 indicates: "Laws that directly affect cultural, use of language, education, personal documentation, and use of symbols, as well as laws on local finances, local elections, the city of Skopje, and boundaries of municipalities, must receive a majority of votes, within which there must be a majority of the votes of the representatives claiming to belong to the community, not in the majority in the population of Macedonia." General, was the need for an amendment of the legislation dealing with issues of national minorities foreseen also in the Prizren and communique number 6?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall every detail, but this is in force now and in practice in the Republic of Macedonia, this demand.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. And, finally, item 6 mentions: "Education and the use of language."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we go to item 6.5, which, in English, it's the very bottom of the document, and I believe in the Macedonian version we have to go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Item 6.5, General, indicates: "Any other language spoken by at least 20 per cent of the population is also an official language, as set forth herein." General, was the demand of the Albanian language, as well as the language of other minorities become an official language, was this demand included within the Prizren agreement.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, finally, if we could go to the next page in English, item 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we see that the Ohrid Agreement indicates that, as annexes of this agreement, there are: "A, constitutional amendments; and, B, legislative modifications." General was the communique number 6, as well as the Prizren agreement, indeed demanding for legislative and constitutional changes?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, would the Ohrid Agreement reflect the NLA demands, goals which have seen both in the Prizren agreement and in communique number 6?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point, I will seek to tender the Prizren agreement and communique number 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I would like to object that these documents be received in evidence. First of all, I would like to address the Prizren agreement, which was shown by the Prosecution. This, as far as we could see, is not authorised, it is not signed by the above mentioned persons, there is no date as to when the agreement was made and, in effect, the witness now gave evidence on behalf of the signatories of this document. We have no such evidence from the person who is are signatories to this agreement. As for communique number 6, which my colleague is now tendering into evidence, as far as I recall the evidence of this witness -- his evidence was that this was prepared by their political leader, Mr. Ali Ahmeti. The document which I see before me, it states on the bottom that it was prepared by the General Staff. The same document is without a date, and has no proof that it comes from -- from the NLA. There is no archive number to which my colleague also alluded to in her questioning, that the documents contained register numbers, archive numbers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We'd simply join our colleague, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your honour. This documents, Your Honour, as I mentioned, were given to us by the witness during proofing, as well as the prior communiques were given to us as well when the statement was taken. I believe that with regards to the communiques, the -- the structure is exactly the same; and in some cases, the communiques did not have the date, and we had to explore that point with the witness. And, Your Honour, with regards to the Prizren agreement, I believe that my colleague is mentioning that there is no date to that in the document itself. If you wish, Your Honour, I can explore with the witness why is that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber will receive communique number 6, which has been confirmed as to its authenticity by the witness. As the Chamber understands the evidence of the witness, he is not in a position to personally authenticate the document labelled the Prizren Agreement and it will not receive that. Communique number 6 is received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P520, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, you will be pleased to know that that concludes the questions that will be asked of you. The point is reached where you will be free to now return to your normal activities. The Chamber would thank you for your attendance here in The Hague and for the assistance that have you been able to give. The court officer will be able to show you out. Thank you, indeed, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Good day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, the Prosecution would call Mr. Thomas Kuehnel. While I'm on my feet, I have a sad duty today, Your Honour. The Prosecution, as you know, has been very ably assisted by the contribution of Ms. Motoike during the proceedings to date. But for reasons of family, Ms. Motoike will be returning to the United States in the near future, So she may not appear again in this case after this week. Fortunately, we are joined today by Ms. Antoinette Issa, an attorney from Quebec, who will be leading the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Saxon, the Chamber would certainly want to join with you in acknowledging the assistance and contribution of Ms. Motoike and wishing her well in her life back in her home country. We notice it's becoming almost a habit, Mr. Saxon, that you're having to inform the Chamber of these things, and we appreciate how much that is putting an additional strain upon you and the remaining members of the team, but we certainly want to send with her the Chamber's wishes for the future. We would welcome also Ms. Issa, who comes now. I don't believe we have had a Canadian counsel in this case, so it's a new element and a new dimension. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply on behalf of the Defence of Mr. Boskoski, we would also wish to joining good luck to Ms. Motoike to her career and life back home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on behalf of the Defence of Mr. Johan Tarculovski, I wish all the best to my learned friend Ms. Motoike. I was glad that we worked together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Apostolski. We would anticipate, therefore, that Ms. Motoike has no need to appear again here, if it is not until a few days that she has to go, but she is welcome if she has nothing more useful to do, to come to court.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I believe the next witness is ready, Mr. Saxon. Could you get Mr. Kuehnel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, please sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa will be asking some questions of you, Mr. Kuehnel. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour. Examination by Ms. Issa

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kuehnel.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honour, before I start, we would like to distribute some binders that relate to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think, Ms. Issa, you take the prize for producing the heaviest single volume.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That was not my intention, Your Honour, but thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do I take it that Defence counsel have their necessary copies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Your Honour, due to the volume of the material, the copies were not provided to the Defence; however, they were given a list of the exhibits that we intend to use. We will also be calling up the exhibits in e-court in order to assist the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, we will see whether that works adequately there practice. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, just for the record, could you please spell your last name. Your name is Thomas Kuehnel, as I understand?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: That's correct. My name is Thomas Kuehnel, K-U-E-H-N-E-L.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And you are an investigator working for the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: When did you begin your work with the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I started to work for the Office of the Prosecutor in October 2003.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And if you can just very briefly tell us, where did you work prior to commencing your work with the Office of the Prosecutor in 2003?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I worked with the German police force and -- in Bavaria.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: For how long?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Since about, now, including this time, 26 years. I started in September 1982.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And can you briefly explain what was your role on this case, before the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: At the beginning of my duty for the OTP, I worked as a P-2 investigator in the OTP in Team C; and from the beginning of my assignment, I started to work on the case of Ljuboten. I was a team member among three other investigators, and that's basically my role.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm just going start off with 65 ter exhibit 280, if we can call that up, please. It's at tab 1 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, this is an RFA from the OTP to the government of Macedonia, which is dated July 8, 2005. I draw your attention to paragraph 2 of the RFA --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: -- which requests the following: "Please also advise whether the Macedonian army units or departments supplied soldiers or weaponry or other equipment to the ground forces (referred to above) that entered the village," and that's the village of Ljuboten, "on 12 August 2001, under the general direction of Johan Tarculovski."

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please call up 65 ter Exhibit 321 at tab 2 of the binders.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I refer your -- just to draw your attention to paragraph 2 which says: "Units of the army..." This is a response from the Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Defence, which is dated 5 September 1995, in response to that RFA. It refers and states in paragraph 2 --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Actually, I will start with paragraph 1: "Units or individuals of the army of the Republic of Macedonia did not take part in the land operation over the village of Ljuboten, which was under the leadership of Johan Tarculovski on 12 August 2001." Then continuing on paragraph 2, it states: "Units of the army of the Republic of Macedonia have not been providing soldiers, weapons, or other equipment for the land forces that entered the village of Ljuboten on 12 August 2001, under main leadership by Johan Tarculovski."

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I see that Mr. Mettraux is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise for stopping it at this stage, but the Defence of Mr. Boskoski would simple like to obtain a indication as to whether Mr. Kuehnel was the author of the first letter which was shown to him, or whether he was the recipient of the second letter that is now being shown. An answer to those questions could, Your Honour, be relevant, we submit, as to whether the witness could be asked questions in relation to that particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that they are the only two bases upon which he might give evidence about them?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we believe that there may be some limitation about the nature ... [Albanian on English Channel] ... to the witness whether he would have received the material or whether he has reviewed the material, in particular, because our understanding would be that, for instance, the witness would not be permitted to give evidence about material that was, for example, summarized or about the circumstances in which a document was obtained, if he did not himself obtain that material. We simply want to be able to know what can be asked of this witness, in light of the information which we sought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So far, the Chamber is not in a position to know where you're going on what you're intending to be asking. So in light of the matters being raised by Mr. Mettraux, we would ask you to consider whether you need to secure any more information from the witness before proceeding with your questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I can do that, Your Honour, but it would be my submission that I -- I would generally be permitted to ask him questions about material that he is not the author of or recipient of, given that hearsay is admissible in this jurisdiction. So in my respectful submission --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The question is, and that was the point of my comment to Mr. Mettraux, he may be familiar with this whatever it is you're going to ask because he was the author of the letter or the recipient of a reply, but he may also be familiar with it on other bases, including being the investigator who had constant familiarity with the trial and the preparation for it and the correspondence that came and went, and there are a number of other possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would be of use, I suggest, if we knew on what basis the witness is speaking about whatever it is you're going to ask him about.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, regarding the information that I just referred to, the RFA as well as the response that was received in -- in response to that RFA, were you aware of this particular information?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen it. The RFA was sent by our team, by our trial attorney. I see my name on that the RFA, and for sure I have read the answers which we received as a team. Yes, I did see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And when you say you "received it as a team," can you explain briefly what specifically you're referring to, just to clarify?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Well, RFAs are sent out by always signed by the or drafted by the trial attorneys, and you can see, for example, on the last page of this RFA that my name was also mentioned together with the trial attorney's name, so I speak about the Prosecution team.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Turning, then, to the next document at tab 3 of the binders, which is 65 ter 283.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: This is another Request for Assistance or RFA.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I would just like to draw your attention to what is marked as paragraph 1 under 1?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Correct. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And the request is for the following: "Please advise if any individual of non-Albanian ethnic, whether a member of the Macedonian security forces or not, was investigated, indicted, prosecuted, or proceeded against by any other measure by the state prosecuting court or any other judicial authorities for any crimes arising out of events occurring in Ljuboten village from 10 to 12 August 2001, or out of events connected to the imprisonment and mistreatment of Albanian detainees who were in custody during the period 12 to 15 August 2001." It lists a number of locations. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that RFA is dated 8 July 2005, for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can please turn to page 2 of the RFA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Just to draw your attention to what is marked as paragraph 4, which states or which reads: "Please also advise if Johan Tarculovski or Ljube Boskoski or anyone acting on their behalf referred any individual or group of individuals of non-Albanian ethnicity or any other person, whether a member of the Macedonian security forces or not, to the state prosecuting court or any other judicial authorities to be investigated, indicted, prosecuted, or proceeded against by any other measure for suspicion of involvement in any crimes arising out of events occurring in Ljuboten village from 10 to 12 August 2001, or out the events connected to the imprisonment and mistreatment of Albanian detainees who were in custody from or during 12 to 15 August at the locations that were in 1 to 9 above." Were you aware of this particular request, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Turning then your attention to tab 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: In the hard copy in the binder, it's 65 ter 283.1, at page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I just draw your attention to paragraph 2, the second paragraph on that page, which states: "Regarding the request, the Ministry took the appropriate examinations within its competence and through its organisational units, concerning the event Ljuboten in the period from 10 August to 12 August 2001. The results show that no non-Albanian individual is the subject of a criminal investigation, indictment, or any other procedure in connection with the events that took place in the above mentioned period." That is a letter addressed to the OTP from Besim Ramicevic, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes. He is our liaison officer within the Ministry of Interior for the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And if we look at page 1 at the top, the cover page, that is dated September 22, 2005. Do you see that, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just the last document in this series, at tab 5 in the binders, 65 ter 382, which also appears to be a response to the RFA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we look at the first page, the date on that is 11 -- November 2nd, 2005, from the Republic of Macedonia to the Office of the Prosecutor. I draw your attention to page 2, please, of that document. At the very bottom, it's a letter to the Republic of Macedonia from the assistant to the minister, head of the SVR Skopje, Lase Velkovski [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And at the very bottom of that paragraph, that single paragraph, it reads: "We would like to inform you that no investigation, indictment, criminal prosecution, or other procedure by the public prosecutions office and the court has been initiated against any person of non-Albanian entity." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And were you aware of this information?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Then if we can just mover to 65 ter 628, please, at tab 6 of the binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: That's another RFA, I don't propose to read it. Do you recognise that, that RFA, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And it's requesting access -- a physical access to the archives for submitted criminal charges. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can question please turn to tab 7, 65 ter 356.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document in front of you, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can you explain what that document is?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I see here the English version of a printout from the so-called crime register of the Macedonian Ministry of Interior, and this relates to the chapter 34 of this crime registry. Chapter 34 is, at the same time, the same of the chapter 34 of the Macedonian Criminal Code.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. If I can stop you there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Sorry. If I can stop you there for a moment. Can you, first of all, explain where you obtained this document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I obtained this document from the Ministry of Interior, where I have been on that day, where I seized it in the presence of the head of the -- I think it was the analytical -- or no, archive sector. I just can't remember the name of the lady. Could you remind me?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Well, at the very -- I believe at the -- if I can help assist you in refreshing your memory? It's a Mrs. Arsovska?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yeah, that is correct. I was in the presence of Mrs. Arsovska when she did her search on her database, and you can also see under number 3 that it refers to the area of Skopje. The search was done in this chapter 34, which is also basically known as war crimes. This sector covers the Criminal Code.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So if I could, just to clarify, to stop you there, Mr. Kuehnel. You requested this search from Mrs. Arsovska. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yeah, that is correct. I did that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters and the court reporter kindly ask the witness and Prosecutor to pause between question and answer and enable us to do our work.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And did you, Mr. Kuehnel, request -- make a specific request to Mrs. Arsovska?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I asked her to conduct a search for me, to see if there was any war crime record in this -- in this crime register visible.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. So you asked her to conduct a search in -- to find out if there were any war crimes initiated in what we're looking at at SVR Skopje?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And for what year did you ask her to conduct the search?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: For the year 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And you mentioned earlier chapter 34 of the Criminal Code?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Is that the chapter that refers to -- of Macedonia -- the Criminal Code of Macedonia which refers to the section on war crimes?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review this document, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I received these documents in my hands, and I refute them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And based on your review of this document, did you find any criminal charges related to war crimes filed against anybody in the SVR --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: -- Skopje in 2001?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: My Apologies. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This is the documents that are at tab 7. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not clear whether they are entered in the electronic system as one document or as a number of documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I believe they're entered into the electronic system as one document, and I can provide the ERN numbers if that assists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: The ERN number is N002-3399 to N002-3418. If it just assists the Chamber, for the purposes of the hard copy that was placed in the binder, only the first ten pages are provided in the hard copy, but the entire document should be in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P521, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, if I can move on to the next exhibit, that's 65 ter 355 at tab 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Once again, Mr. Kuehnel, if you can look at page 1 of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: It also appears to be an exhibit from a crime register?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: With all due respect, the interpreters need to ask again the witness and the counsel to pause for a moment between the question and answer, as our language is much less concise than the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We will do our best to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It becomes necessary to undergo a personal slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We all have to go through the experience, but the necessity of multi-language interpretation requires us just to pause a lot, think a lot, and speak slowly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And that is so both for counsel and for witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: We will take that instruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I suspect that you will rapidly fall into your former habit, and we may have to mention it once or twice again before it becomes a habit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. I will do my best not to allow that to happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, just returning to 65 ter 355, which is the results of the computer search for criminal records, can you -- you indicated you recognised it. Did you obtain this document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, I obtained this document. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you obtain it at the same time as you obtained the previous document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I did. I did obtain it on the same day, but I did obtain it at a different time and from a different person.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And where did you obtain it from?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: This document I obtained from the liaison officer, Besim Ramicevic, who made the same type of search like the previous documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And what -- what is different about this document than the previous document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: The search is exactly the same. The difference is that Mr. Besim Ramicevic had a different access to the system, and he made a countrywide search for the same purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So if I can summarize what you have said, he, Mr. Ramicevic, did a countrywide search, as opposed to the search which was done previously, which was only for the SVR Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And this also relates to a search of whether or not war crimes were charged in the country, and was it in the same year 2001?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Either it refers to the same subject, also the search for chapter 34; and was the same year, which is under number 2, for the year 2001. That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if I can please ask Madam Registrar to turn to page 6 of the English translation, and also in the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Drawing your attention, Mr. Kuehnel, to page 6. Did you learn of any case of any alleged war crime during the year 2001?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I have. I see here one search result and it's described as racial and other discrimination, and the place of the crime was Kumanovo in the year 2001, 7th of August. This is basically the information I can see here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you receive any further information concerning this crime from anyone?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: No, not to this particular crime.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: All right. Referring then to page 4 of the same document, and drawing your attention to the reference to human trafficking --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you. And apart from these cases, based on your review of the documents, did you find any other cases of persons charged with war crimes in the Republic of Macedonia in the year 2001?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, I believe that you recently were involved in a search of the archives relating to the permanent commission for disciplinary proceedings for the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.text: And what was the purpose of your -- of the archive search?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. So your purpose was to determine whether any disciplinary proceedings had been initiated against any member of the MOI involved in the Ljuboten events. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And when you attended at the archive, did you meet with anybody there?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I met with several persons. The main contact person was introduced to me as Mrs. Naumova.

utterances.text: And who was Mrs. Naumova? What was her title?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Mrs. Naumova was the head of the human-- hang on. What was it? I think it was the legal department or human resource department. Can you remind me a moment, please, in my note. I recorded it in my note.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. And the note you are referring to, for the record, is at tab 10 in the binder --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: -- and it is not listed on the 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Mrs. Naumova provide with you any documentation regarding disciplinary proceedings carried out in 2001 and 2002?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, she did. Based on my request, I asked Mrs. Naumova to provide me with an overview about all disciplinary proceedings in the year 2001 and in the year 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And turning, then, to tab 11, at 65 ter number 1058.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd just like to call that up on the screen, first. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER

utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kuehnel, did you learn at some point how these lists of disciplinary proceedings that we just reviewed were compiled?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you have an opportunity, Mr. Kuehnel, to do a search or review of the cases recorded in 2001 or 2002?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes. I had this opportunity, and I started to do this review based on these two lists and the information I could read on these lists about all these cases from 2001 and 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And in any of the cases, in 2001 or 2002, was any member of the Ministry of Interior investigated, disciplined, or punished for any misconduct relating to the events in Ljuboten in August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you, Mr. Kuehnel, in a moment as to what steps you took to review these cases, but I first would like you -- would like to deal with the organisational structure of the disciplinary commission. utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If this issue had to be dealt with, we believe that it could have and should have been raised with witnesses that have that expertise, in particular, and I've indicated already Mr. Galevski who was not asked those questions or Ms. Rusovska for that matter. We believe that this is not proper evidence to be asked of an investigator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, as you may or may not here in a moment, Mr. Kuehnel was in a position to learn about the organisational structure from an individual at the -- who works at the archive, who is the head of the legal department, Mrs. Naumova, and who explained to him how the disciplinary commission is organised. He can, in my respectful submission, provide that evidence without having to provide an opinion of sorts on it. As Mr. Mettraux knows, he is not here to provide an opinion. He is simply providing evidence as to what he was informed by Mrs. Naumova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please continue, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you learn at some stage, Mr. Kuehnel, as to how the Permanent Disciplinary Committee was established?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. Yes, I learned about that. I was asking Mrs. Naumova to give me an overview about the disciplinary body, and the first what I learned was that the disciplinary body is consisting based on the collective work agreement, as a legal source, and that this disciplinary body is not an institution by itself. It comprises out of several commissions which are founded and appointed, based on the collective work agreement, and formed according to the organisational structure of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Now --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can you explain the organisational structure of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The organisational structure of the Ministry of Interior is, what I learned, a mixture between a regional structure and an organisational structure, which means basically that one commission is founded for each regional SVR of the Ministry of Interior, and commissions are also founded for different areas within the Ministry of Interior. Now, in general words, this structure is consistent over other the years. Also, the organisational structure of the Ministry of Interior changed in parts, which means, for example, that the number of the SVRs changed in the year 2001. I was informed there were 12 regional SVRs. Currently, there are eight. This means that there are eight commissions for eight SVR; and so it was in 2001, there were 12 commissions for 12 SVRs. Additionally, there are commissions for the so-called centralised police units of the Ministry of Interior, the MOI units; and, as a sort of special organisation formed, there was an extra commission for the intelligence service of the Ministry of Interior and the border police units. Each commission consists out of three members, which are always appointed by the decision of the minister for the duration of two years. The commission consists of the president of the commission and two members. I was told that the commission works independently and will be replaced after two years of time when the particular time of this commission expires. That means, not at the same time, the whole commission -- all commissions are replaced, because time by time --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I think have -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: No, no. I think I explained the structure as such.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I see Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I am grateful. Simply a clarification, if the colleague could seek it from the witness, perhaps the time-period which the witness discussed in particular in the second part of his answer, where he listed a number of commissions and whether this is the evidence of Mr. Kuehnel, that this is, in fact, the structure as of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I can attempt to clarify that, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, I believe you mentioned that, in 2001, there were 12 commissions; and, subsequently, that was changed to, I believe, you said eight.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Would you -- could you elaborate on your response -- on that answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes. I referred with number of 12 commissions for the 12 SVRs of the Ministry of Interior. This was the information I received.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And was that in the year 2001?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And just to be perfectly clear, you indicated that this has changed since then, the number of commissions?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes. As far as what I received as information, what I could see was that we have -- the MOI has currently eight SVRs.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, it was probably my objection, so that wasn't very clear, but it related to the so-called special commissions that Mr. Kuehnel indicated whether it is his evidence that those existed in the year 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'll clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, did the commissions that related -- or that excluded the border police and the DBK -- or that were attached to the border police and the DBK, that those existed in 2001, were you given any information in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: That was my understanding, yes, that they existed in 2001. And by "special," I mean only that they had its own commission of its for own unit, also they belonged inside the MOI structure. This is only a term in reference to the organisation of the MOI, and this was the way how I got it explained.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So if I understand, what you're saying is that the border police and the DBK each had their own commissions. Is that correct? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: That's correct. I understood it in this way. It was explained to me in this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Turning, then, to tab 14 which is 65 ter 1060, If I can ask that that be called up, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recognise that document, Mr. Kuehnel, that's in front of you? The Macedonian version is also on e-court, which should appear before you now.

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And how did you obtain that document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: In the same way as I received the other documents, I received this from Mrs. Naumova from the MOI. I asked for decisions of establishing a commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And this is a decision for establishing a commission for the different SVRs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that, that this decision refers to the establishing a commission for the SVR Bitola.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And behind that, there are additional decisions establishing commissions for other SVRs, isn't that correct, if you look behind the document?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: I see here only SVR Bitola in my binder. I only see here one page.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And you're looking at the English translation?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: It's the English translation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, perhaps if I can ask for the page 3 to be called up in e-court, please. I'm sorry, could we go to the next page, please. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you see that on your screen, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes. I see this English document on the left side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And that's a decision that is, as it reads, "establishing a commission on the enforcements of proceedings for reaching a decision of termination of employment with a notice of resignation in Sol-Kumanovo in the following composition." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can then move to the next page, please. If it assists, the next ERN number is N006-5551. It should be at page 5 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: That's a decision on "establishing a commission for termination of employment in Sol Stip." "Establishing a commission on enforcement of proceedings for reaching a decision on termination of employment with a notice of resignation in Sol Stip," is the first heading. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we ask the Prosecutor to come closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can then, please, turn to page 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: That's a decision dated at the top, August 23rd, 2002, and it is on the -- it's "establishing a commission for enforcement of proceedings in the region of Prilep." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can please turn to page 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: That's dated July 18, 2002, and it's a decision on "establishing a commission in the ream of Ohrid." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can please just return to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: That's a decision, as you see on your screen on the first page, "establishing a commission in Bitola on the 20th of June, 2001." Do you see that there, Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like to tendered this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P525, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kuehnel, I'd like to deal with the steps that would be taken if a member of the Ministry of Interior was accused of an act of misconduct. Did you learn what type of misconduct would be the subject of disciplinary proceedings within the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I was explained that every misbehaviour of a person against the work regulations would result in disciplinary proceedings and/or in criminal charge, if that is the case. But in reference of disciplinary proceeding, if a violation would be committed by a person, a member of the MOI, it would normally result in a disciplinary proceeding. The disciplinary proceeding consists normally out of four steps of procedure, and I was asking that this proceeding was explained to me, since I was not aware of these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can you explain what those steps are?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The first questions that I had is not really an objection, but the question was whether my colleague could ask the witness to indicate where he said, "I was explained that every misbehaviour," and so on, and whether the witness could identify the person who explained that matter to him. The second matter, Your Honour, is truly an objection. At this stage, the Prosecutor is seeking to elicit evidence of another person through this witness. The Prosecutor is, in effect, attempting to replace the evidence of the person who gave that information to Mr. Kuehnel by the evidence of Mr. Kuehnel itself. This, Your Honour, we submit, would constitute a violation of the principle of best evidence, which requires that the person capable of giving that evidence be called if available. The Prosecution has taken the view not to call that person. We would be prejudiced, if required, to cross-examine Mr. Kuehnel on this matter, since our ability to cross-examine would be limited to the fact that Mr. Kuehnel was, in fact, said such things, not whether they were correct or not. We believe that the law of this Tribunal is quite clear about, as far as we understand it, as far as the type of evidence which may be elicited from the witness, and also and in particular the fact that the rules on admission of evidence cannot simply be disregarded, in particular Rule 92 busy and 92 ter which would entitle us to cross-examine the person who is the source of that evidence. I believe at this stage, Your Honour, that we have passed the stage the line where Mr. Kuehnel can legitimately be asked a questions about this matter. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux's objection is essentially similar to the one that he made earlier, Your Honour, in that, in my view, he is essentially objecting to the hearsay nature of Mr. Kuehnel's evidence. Once again, I would like do submit that the fact that Mr. Kuehnel is testifying about matters that he heard from other persons or, in this case, one other person, or he learned from one other person, does not go to its admission, but, rather, to the weight of the evidence. So, in my submission, this particular portion of Mr. Kuehnel's testimony is no different than what he was testifying to earlier, when the evidence was elicited and admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In the view of the Chamber, the witness is dealing simply with a general system; and, as such, the line of questioning is proper and appropriate. Please continue, Ms. Issa. I saw your eye look to the time, and it is nearly the hour. Is there a matter you want to conclude now or is this a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I might just follow up on Mr. Mettraux's question, just for the sake of completeness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel, you indicated that this was explained to you. Was it the same person who explained to you these matters, Mrs. Naumova?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS Kuehnel
utterances.text: Yes, it was basically Mrs. Naumova. I was mainly, among other persons, I met on this day, speaking of these days, Mrs. Naumova, and she actually explained me all the things I can testify here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you.
